Definition: to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application
BiblicalUsage: To do or make is the commonest verb in the Old Testament, and it is used for God's work first of all. God says let us make man in our image, He rests on the seventh day from all His work which He had made, the commandment says in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and the Preacher says whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'to make' is the first thing God tells us about Himself: He is the Maker, and everything else is made. His work does not wear out and does not need adding to, and I hold that our making only matters when it answers His, doing what He has given us to do and resting when He rests.
